answer: Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 36% of the attester's bond. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the tundra registry records each claim and the pulse audit publishes every slash. A farm must therefore either lie, which the pigment graph proves on replay, or recruit 40 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 10 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
